findings.location: Completion criteria 2; Increment B steps 2–3; Increment D step 1
findings.problem: The plan permits a judge to fail parsing twice and records that as a failure, but completion criterion 2 still requires both judges to have rated every pair. It also never defines how failed pairs are excluded or represented in agreement, label-share, tercile, band, gap, or rank calculations. Consequently the required figures can be ambiguous or impossible to produce when any permitted failure occurs.
findings.suggestion: Define a valid-rating denominator for every statistic; state that failures are reported separately and excluded from label-based measures (or assign a specified missing category); revise completion criterion 2 to require an outcome—valid rating or recorded failure—for every pair.

findings.problem: The 20 owner-rated pairs are selected before the 30 Codex pairs, and the Codex sample is subsequently selected only by local-judge label strata. Nothing requires overlap with the owner sample. The promised Codex-versus-owner agreement can therefore have zero observations, despite being a stated completion result and part of the goal of knowing the judges’ trust.
findings.suggestion: Reserve or deliberately include owner-rated pairs in the Codex selection, while preserving the stated strata, and specify the minimum overlap and how any short stratum is handled.

summary: The plan is well scoped, but two permitted sampling/error paths leave required trust and analysis results undefined.
